say: You give it a circle with a diameter and a point on the circle. It finds an unknown **angle** and says why it is true.
The key idea: join any point on the circle to the two ends of a diameter and the angle at that point is always $90^\circ$. The diameter is the one thing to look for.

how.higher: At Higher it is a step inside a longer Paper 2 geometry part (2016, 2022, 2024): you state the $90^\circ$ at the diameter and use it to reach the other angles or to finish a proof.
how.ordinary: At Ordinary it appeared in 2022 Paper 2, in a 5-mark part that asks for the angle in a semicircle on its own, then an angle found from it.

example.question: $[AB]$ is a diameter of a circle and $C$ is a point on the circle. $|\angle CAB| = 38^\circ$. Find $|\angle ABC|$.

steps.title: Spot the diameter
steps.say: $[AB]$ is a diameter, so $C$ makes an angle in a semicircle. By Corollary 3 that angle is $\hl{1}{90^\circ}$.

steps.title: Use the angle sum
steps.say: The angles in triangle $ABC$ add to $180^\circ$. Write them in, with $x$ for the angle we want.

steps.title: Solve for x
steps.say: Add the two known angles, then take them from $180$.

Indicating the $90^\circ$ at the diameter is partial credit on its own, so write it down first even if you stall later.
When a reason is asked for, any valid one scores. Naming this corollary is one of the accepted answers.

ordinary.tip: Finding the angle in a semicircle is hit or miss: $90^\circ$ gets the marks and nothing else does.

say: You give it two triangles and some equal sides and angles. It shows the triangles are **congruent** and names the case that proves it.
The key idea: you do not need all six matches. Three of the right kind (SSS, SAS, ASA or RHS) are enough, and each match needs a reason.

how.higher: At Higher it is a step inside longer Paper 2 proofs (2015, 2021, 2023, 2024, 2025): you prove two triangles congruent, usually by ASA, so that a side or angle can be used later.
how.ordinary: At Ordinary it is tested most years on Paper 2 (2015, 2018, 2022, 2025): explain or prove two triangles congruent, or say whether a claim about them is true, for 5 to 15 marks.

example.question: In the quadrilateral $ABCD$, $|AB| = |AD| = 5$ cm and $|BC| = |DC| = 7$ cm. Prove that $\Delta ABC$ and $\Delta ADC$ are congruent.

steps.title: Pick the two triangles
steps.say: The diagonal $[AC]$ cuts the figure into $\Delta ABC$ and $\Delta ADC$. Compare them one pair of parts at a time.

lines.text: Match the vertices in order: $A$ with $A$, $B$ with $D$, $C$ with $C$.

steps.title: Match the first two pairs
steps.say: Write each pair of equal sides, with its reason beside it.

steps.title: Find the shared side
steps.say: Both triangles contain $\hl{2}{[AC]}$. A side in both triangles is equal to itself.

steps.title: Name the case and conclude
steps.say: Three pairs of equal sides is the case $\hl{1}{\text{SSS}}$. State the conclusion with the case as the reason.

higher.tip: Put a reason beside every statement, such as "vertically opposite" or "alternate angles". The scheme lists them line by line.
A side shared by both triangles needs writing down as equal to itself, with the reason "common side".
More than one proof is accepted, so use the case you can justify. Any valid proof scores.

ordinary.tip: End with a conclusion and give a reason for each step. Leaving either out costs a mark.
Full marks need three statements and three reasons: three matching pairs, each with its reason.
Even naming a case (SSS, SAS, RHS or ASA) earns partial credit, so always name one.
Mark the equal parts on the diagram. A diagram with three of them marked is credited.

say: You give it an object, a centre $O$ and a **scale factor** $k$. It draws the image, or finds $k$ from two lengths, or finds the new area.
The key idea: every length is multiplied by $k$ but every area is multiplied by $k^2$.

how.higher: At Higher it was a step inside a 2025 Paper 2 geometry question: find the scale factor, then use it to find an area of the image.
how.ordinary: At Ordinary it is tested almost every year (2015, 2017, 2021, 2022, 2024) on Paper 2: find $k$ from two lengths, find a missing length, find an area, or construct the image from the centre.

example.question: The triangle $ABC$ is enlarged with centre $O$ to give the image $PQR$. $|OB| = 5$ cm and $|OQ| = 12$ cm. The area of $ABC$ is $10$ cm$^2$. Find the area of $PQR$.

steps.title: Find the scale factor
steps.say: The scale factor is image length over object length. Use the two lengths from $O$: $\hl{1}{k} = \frac{|OQ|}{|OB|}$.

steps.title: Square the scale factor
steps.say: Lengths grow by $k$, so areas grow by $\hl{2}{k^2}$.

ordinary.tip: The scheme splits a scale-factor question into items: find $k$, find the first length, find the second. Each is a step the marks follow.
For an area, square $k$ before you multiply. Squaring $k$ or multiplying by $k$ is already work of merit.

say: You give it a parallelogram with some angles or sides as numbers or expressions. It finds the unknown and names the reason.
The key idea: **opposite** sides are equal and **opposite** angles are equal. Angles side by side (adjacent) add to $180^\circ$.
what.out: unknown angle or side, with reason

how.higher: At Higher it is never the main skill of a part. It is a step inside longer Paper 2 proofs (2015, 2018, 2023, 2024), for example to say opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal.
how.ordinary: At Ordinary it is tested on Paper 2 (2016, 2018, 2023): find angles in a parallelogram for 5 marks, or write statements with reasons about its sides and angles for 10.

example.question: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram. $|\angle DAB| = (2x + 15)^\circ$ and $|\angle BCD| = (4x - 35)^\circ$. Find $|\angle ABC|$.

steps.title: Equal opposite angles
steps.say: $\angle DAB$ and $\angle BCD$ are opposite angles. By Theorem 9 opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, so put the two expressions equal.

steps.title: Solve for x
steps.say: Collect the $x$ terms on one side and the numbers on the other.

steps.title: Find angle DAB
steps.say: Put $\hl{1}{x = 25}$ into the expression for $\angle DAB$.

steps.title: Use adjacent angles
steps.say: $\angle ABC$ is next to $\angle DAB$. Adjacent angles in a parallelogram add to $180^\circ$, so take $\hl{2}{65}$ from $180$.

ordinary.tip: Give each fact as a statement and a reason. Full credit needs three statements and three reasons.
